steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Inference means using evidence from the text AND your own reasoning to work out meanings that are NOT directly stated. You "read between the lines." | PEE Structure: P oint - State your inference E vidence - Quote from the text E xplain - Show how the evidence proves your point | Inference Exam Strategy: Always use the PEE structure - Point, Evidence, Explanation. Your point should state the inferred meaning clearly, your evidence must be a short quotation, and your explanation must show HOW the evidence leads to your inference. For AQA Paper 1 Q2 and Paper 2 Q3, spend 10-12 minutes. Examiners reward specific, well-supported inferences over vague guesses. Always ask yourself: "What does this word/phrase suggest, and how do I know?"
